title: Concentration Terms (Molarity, Molality, Mole Fraction, Mass Percentage, & ppm)
syllabus: Methods of expressing concentration of solutions: Mass percentage (w/w), Volume percentage (v/v), Mass by volume percentage (w/v), Parts per million (ppm), Parts per billion (ppb); Mole fraction (X), Molarity (M), Molality (m), Normality (N), Formality; Temperature dependence of concentration terms (temperature-dependent vs temperature-independent units); Dilution law and mixing of solutions (M1V1 = M2V2, M_mix = (M1V1 + M2V2)/(V1 + V2)); Interconversion between concentration terms (Molarity to Molality, Mole fraction to Molality, Mass percent and density to Molarity); Standard solutions and quantitative solution stoichiometry

questions.question: [NEET 2023] Which of the following concentration terms is temperature-independent?
questions.solution:
1. Concentration terms that involve the volume of the solution (such as Molarity, Normality, and Volume percentage) depend on temperature because liquids expand or contract upon temperature variation ($V \propto T$).
2. Concentration terms that depend exclusively on the mass of the solute and mass of the solvent/solution (such as Molality, Mole fraction, Mass percentage, and ppm by mass) are completely temperature-independent, as mass does not change with temperature.
Therefore, **Molality** is independent of temperature.

questions.question: [NEET 2022] Concentrated aqueous sulfuric acid is commercially sold as $98\%\ \text{H}_2\text{SO}_4$ by mass with a density of $1.84\text{ g/mL}$. The molarity of the acid solution is: (Molar mass of $\text{H}_2\text{SO}_4 = 98.0\text{ g/mol}$)
questions.solution:
Using the standard direct relationship between molarity ($M$), mass percentage ($x\%$), and density ($d\text{ in g/mL}$):
$$M = \frac{x \times d \times 10}{M_w}$$
Substitute $x = 98$, $d = 1.84\text{ g/mL}$, and $M_w = 98.0\text{ g/mol}$:
$$M = \frac{98 \times 1.84 \times 10}{98.0} = 1.84 \times 10 = 18.4\text{ M}$$

questions.question: [NEET 2021] What is the mole fraction of ethylene glycol ($\text{C}_2\text{H}_6\text{O}_2$) in an aqueous solution containing $20\%\ \text{C}_2\text{H}_6\text{O}_2$ by mass? (Molar masses: $\text{C}_2\text{H}_6\text{O}_2 = 62.0\text{ g/mol}, \text{H}_2\text{O} = 18.0\text{ g/mol}$)
questions.solution:
Consider $100\text{ g}$ of the solution:
1. Mass of $\text{C}_2\text{H}_6\text{O}_2 = 20\text{ g}$.
2. Mass of water $= 100 - 20 = 80\text{ g}$.
3. Moles of each component:
$$n_{\text{glycol}} = \frac{20\text{ g}}{62.0\text{ g/mol}} \approx 0.3226\text{ mol}$$
$$n_{\text{H}_2\text{O}} = \frac{80\text{ g}}{18.0\text{ g/mol}} \approx 4.4444\text{ mol}$$
4. Mole fraction of glycol:
$$X_{\text{glycol}} = \frac{n_{\text{glycol}}}{n_{\text{glycol}} + n_{\text{H}_2\text{O}}} = \frac{0.3226}{0.3226 + 4.4444} = \frac{0.3226}{4.767} \approx 0.06767 \approx 0.068$$

questions.question: [NEET 2020] When $250\text{ mL}$ of $0.5\text{ M } \text{HCl}$ is mixed with $750\text{ mL}$ of $0.1\text{ M } \text{HCl}$, assuming volumes are additive, the molarity of the resulting mixture is:
questions.solution:
Using the mixing equation for non-reacting solutions of the same solute:
$$M_1 V_1 + M_2 V_2 = M_{\text{mix}} V_{\text{total}}$$
1. Calculate millimoles of $\text{HCl}$ from each solution:
$$\text{mmol}_1 = 250\text{ mL} \times 0.5\text{ M} = 125\text{ mmol}$$
$$\text{mmol}_2 = 750\text{ mL} \times 0.1\text{ M} = 75\text{ mmol}$$
$$\text{Total mmol} = 125 + 75 = 200\text{ mmol}$$
2. Total volume of mixture:
$$V_{\text{total}} = 250 + 750 = 1000\text{ mL}$$
3. Molarity of mixture:
$$M_{\text{mix}} = \frac{\text{Total mmol}}{V_{\text{total in mL}}} = \frac{200}{1000} = 0.20\text{ M}$$

questions.question: [NEET 2023] A sample of drinking water was found to be severely contaminated with chloroform ($\text{CHCl}_3$), a suspected carcinogen. The level of contamination was $15\text{ ppm}$ by mass. What is this concentration expressed as a mass percentage?
questions.solution:
By definition:
$$\text{ppm} = \frac{\text{Mass of solute}}{\text{Mass of solution}} \times 10^6$$
$$\%\text{ by mass} = \frac{\text{Mass of solute}}{\text{Mass of solution}} \times 100$$
Therefore:
$$\%\text{ by mass} = \frac{\text{ppm}}{10^4} = \frac{15}{10^4} = 1.5 \times 10^{-3}\%$$

questions.question: [NEET 2022] The molarity of pure liquid water at $4^\circ\text{C}$ (density $= 1.00\text{ g/mL}$) is:
questions.solution:
Consider $1.00\text{ L}$ ($1000\text{ mL}$) of pure water:
1. Mass of $1000\text{ mL}$ of water:
$$m = 1000\text{ mL} \times 1.00\text{ g/mL} = 1000\text{ g}$$
2. Moles of water present in $1000\text{ g}$ ($M = 18.016\text{ g/mol} \approx 18.0\text{ g/mol}$):
$$n = \frac{1000\text{ g}}{18.0\text{ g/mol}} = 55.55\text{ moles}$$
3. Molarity:
$$M = \frac{\text{Moles}}{\text{Volume in L}} = \frac{55.55\text{ mol}}{1.00\text{ L}} = 55.55\text{ M}$$

questions.question: [NEET 2021] An aqueous solution contains $3.0\text{ g}$ of urea (molar mass $= 60\text{ g/mol}$) dissolved in $250\text{ g}$ of water. The molality of this solution is:
questions.solution:
1. Moles of urea:
$$n = \frac{\text{Mass}}{\text{Molar mass}} = \frac{3.0\text{ g}}{60\text{ g/mol}} = 0.05\text{ mol}$$
2. Mass of solvent (water) in kilograms:
$$W = \frac{250\text{ g}}{1000} = 0.25\text{ kg}$$
3. Molality ($m$):
$$m = \frac{n}{W} = \frac{0.05\text{ mol}}{0.25\text{ kg}} = 0.20\text{ m}$$

questions.question: [NEET 2023] An aqueous solution of a non-volatile solute has a mole fraction of $0.20$. What is the molality of the solution? (Molar mass of solvent $\text{H}_2\text{O} = 18.0\text{ g/mol}$)
questions.solution:
Using the relation between molality ($m$) and mole fraction of solute ($X_B$):
$$m = \frac{X_B}{1 - X_B} \times \frac{1000}{M_A}$$
where $M_A = 18.0\text{ g/mol}$ (molar mass of water).
Substitute $X_B = 0.20$:
$$m = \frac{0.20}{1 - 0.20} \times \frac{1000}{18} = \frac{0.20}{0.80} \times 55.555$$
$$m = 0.25 \times 55.555 \approx 13.89\text{ m}$$

questions.question: [NEET 2020] What volume of $0.10\text{ M } \text{H}_2\text{SO}_4$ is required to completely neutralize $20.0\text{ mL}$ of $0.20\text{ M } \text{NaOH}$?
questions.solution:
Using the principle of equivalence:
$$N_1 V_1 = N_2 V_2$$
1. For $\text{H}_2\text{SO}_4$ (dibasic acid, $n\text{-factor} = 2$):
$$N_1 = M_1 \times 2 = 0.10 \times 2 = 0.20\text{ N}$$
2. For $\text{NaOH}$ (monoacidic base, $n\text{-factor} = 1$):
$$N_2 = M_2 \times 1 = 0.20 \times 1 = 0.20\text{ N}$$
3. Equating gram equivalents:
$$0.20 \times V_1 = 0.20 \times 20.0\text{ mL}$$
$$V_1 = 20.0\text{ mL}$$

questions.question: [NEET 2022] The density of a $3.0\text{ M}$ solution of $\text{NaCl}$ is $1.25\text{ g/mL}$. The molality of the solution is approximately: (Molar mass of $\text{NaCl} = 58.5\text{ g/mol}$)
questions.solution:
Consider $1.0\text{ L}$ ($1000\text{ mL}$) of the solution:
1. Moles of $\text{NaCl} = 3.0\text{ mol}$.
2. Mass of solute ($\text{NaCl}$):
$$m_{\text{solute}} = 3.0\text{ mol} \times 58.5\text{ g/mol} = 175.5\text{ g}$$
3. Mass of $1000\text{ mL}$ of solution:
$$m_{\text{solution}} = 1000\text{ mL} \times 1.25\text{ g/mL} = 1250.0\text{ g}$$
4. Mass of solvent (water):
$$m_{\text{solvent}} = m_{\text{solution}} - m_{\text{solute}} = 1250.0 - 175.5 = 1074.5\text{ g} = 1.0745\text{ kg}$$
5. Molality ($m$):
$$m = \frac{\text{Moles of solute}}{\text{Mass of solvent in kg}} = \frac{3.0\text{ mol}}{1.0745\text{ kg}} \approx 2.792\text{ m} \approx 2.79\text{ m}$$

questions.question: [NEET 2021] If $500\text{ mL}$ of a $0.2\text{ M}$ solution is diluted with water until its final volume becomes $2.0\text{ L}$, the molarity of the resulting diluted solution is:
questions.solution:
Using the dilution equation:
$$M_1 V_1 = M_2 V_2$$
Convert volumes to liters (or consistent units):
- $V_1 = 500\text{ mL} = 0.50\text{ L}$
- $M_1 = 0.2\text{ M}$
- $V_2 = 2.0\text{ L}$
$$0.2 \times 0.50 = M_2 \times 2.0$$
$$0.10 = M_2 \times 2.0 \implies M_2 = \frac{0.10}{2.0} = 0.05\text{ M}$$

questions.question: [NEET 2023] A solution contains $23\text{ g}$ of ethanol ($\text{C}_2\text{H}_5\text{OH}$) and $36\text{ g}$ of water ($\text{H}_2\text{O}$). What is the mole fraction of ethanol in this binary mixture? (Molar masses: $\text{C}_2\text{H}_5\text{OH} = 46\text{ g/mol}, \text{H}_2\text{O} = 18\text{ g/mol}$)
questions.solution:
1. Moles of ethanol:
$$n_{\text{ethanol}} = \frac{23\text{ g}}{46\text{ g/mol}} = 0.5\text{ mol}$$
2. Moles of water:
$$n_{\text{water}} = \frac{36\text{ g}}{18\text{ g/mol}} = 2.0\text{ mol}$$
3. Total moles:
$$n_{\text{total}} = 0.5 + 2.0 = 2.5\text{ mol}$$
4. Mole fraction of ethanol:
$$X_{\text{ethanol}} = \frac{n_{\text{ethanol}}}{n_{\text{total}}} = \frac{0.5}{2.5} = 0.20$$

questions.question: [NEET 2020] An aqueous glucose solution is labeled as $10\%\ (w/v)$. What volume of this solution contains $1.0\text{ mole}$ of glucose? (Molar mass of glucose $= 180\text{ g/mol}$)
questions.solution:
1. A $10\%\ (w/v)$ solution contains $10\text{ g}$ of glucose in every $100\text{ mL}$ of solution.
2. One mole of glucose has a mass of $180\text{ g}$.
3. Using proportionality:
$$\text{Volume} = \frac{100\text{ mL}}{10\text{ g}} \times 180\text{ g} = 1800\text{ mL}$$

questions.question: [NEET 2022] If the hardness of a sample of water is $100\text{ ppm}$ in terms of $\text{CaCO}_3$ equivalent, what is the mass of $\text{CaCO}_3$ present in $10\text{ L}$ of this water sample? (Density of water $= 1.0\text{ g/mL}$)
questions.solution:
1. Mass of $10\text{ L}$ of water:
$$m_{\text{water}} = 10\text{ L} \times 1000\text{ g/L} = 10^4\text{ g}$$
2. By definition of parts per million:
$$\text{ppm} = \frac{\text{Mass of solute}}{\text{Mass of sample}} \times 10^6$$
$$100 = \frac{m_{\text{solute}}}{10^4\text{ g}} \times 10^6$$
$$100 = m_{\text{solute}} \times 100 \implies m_{\text{solute}} = 1.0\text{ g}$$

questions.question: [NEET 2021] A $0.5\text{ M}$ solution of $\text{Al}_2(\text{SO}_4)_3$ is completely dissociated. The molar concentration of sulfate ions ($\text{SO}_4^{2-}$) in the solution is:
questions.solution:
The dissociation equation for aluminum sulfate is:
$$\text{Al}_2(\text{SO}_4)_3(aq) \rightarrow 2\text{Al}^{3+}(aq) + 3\text{SO}_4^{2-}(aq)$$
From the stoichiometry of dissociation:
- $1\text{ formula unit of } \text{Al}_2(\text{SO}_4)_3$ produces $3\text{ sulfate ions}$.
- Therefore, the concentration of sulfate ions is:
$$[\text{SO}_4^{2-}] = 3 \times [\text{Al}_2(\text{SO}_4)_3] = 3 \times 0.5\text{ M} = 1.5\text{ M}$$

questions.question: [NEET 2023] Which of the following statements regarding mole fraction is INCORRECT?
options: Mole fraction depends directly on the temperature of the solution
Mole fraction is a dimensionless quantity with no units
The sum of the mole fractions of all components in a solution is always equal to unity ($1$)
Mole fraction of a pure component is equal to $1$
questions.solution:
1. Mole fraction is defined as the ratio of the number of moles of one component to the total number of moles of all components in the mixture: $X_i = \frac{n_i}{\sum n}$.
2. Because both the numerator and denominator are expressed in moles (which depend strictly on mass and molar mass), mole fraction is completely independent of temperature.
Therefore, Statement A is incorrect.

questions.question: [NEET 2020] An aqueous solution contains $5.85\text{ g}$ of $\text{NaCl}$ per $500\text{ mL}$ of solution. The normality of this solution is: (Molar mass of $\text{NaCl} = 58.5\text{ g/mol}$)
questions.solution:
1. For $\text{NaCl}$, the $n$-factor is $1$ (total positive or negative charge $= 1$), so $\text{Normality} = \text{Molarity}$.
2. Moles of $\text{NaCl}$:
$$n = \frac{5.85\text{ g}}{58.5\text{ g/mol}} = 0.10\text{ mol}$$
3. Volume of solution in liters:
$$V = \frac{500\text{ mL}}{1000} = 0.50\text{ L}$$
4. Molarity and Normality:
$$M = \frac{0.10\text{ mol}}{0.50\text{ L}} = 0.20\text{ M} \implies N = 0.20\text{ N}$$

questions.question: [NEET 2022] A bottle of commercial aqueous $\text{HNO}_3$ contains $63\%\ \text{HNO}_3$ by mass and has a density of $1.40\text{ g/mL}$. The volume of this concentrated acid required to prepare $2.0\text{ L}$ of $0.10\text{ M } \text{HNO}_3$ solution is: (Molar mass of $\text{HNO}_3 = 63.0\text{ g/mol}$)
questions.solution:
1. Find the molarity of the concentrated $\text{HNO}_3$ stock solution:
$$M_1 = \frac{x \times d \times 10}{M_w} = \frac{63 \times 1.40 \times 10}{63.0} = 14.0\text{ M}$$
2. Desired diluted solution:
$$M_2 = 0.10\text{ M}, \quad V_2 = 2.0\text{ L} = 2000\text{ mL}$$
3. Apply the dilution formula:
$$M_1 V_1 = M_2 V_2$$
$$14.0 \times V_1 = 0.10 \times 2000$$
$$14.0 \times V_1 = 200 \implies V_1 = \frac{200}{14.0} \approx 14.285\text{ mL} \approx 14.28\text{ mL}$$

questions.question: [NEET 2021] In a binary solution of two volatile components $A$ and $B$, if the mole fraction of $A$ is $0.30$, what is the mole fraction of $B$?
questions.solution:
For any binary solution, the sum of the mole fractions of all components must equal unity:
$$X_A + X_B = 1$$
Given $X_A = 0.30$:
$$X_B = 1 - 0.30 = 0.70$$

questions.question: [NEET 2023] A sample of blood has a glucose concentration of $90\text{ mg/dL}$. What is the molarity of glucose in this blood sample? (Molar mass of glucose $= 180\text{ g/mol}$)
questions.solution:
1. Note that $1\text{ dL} = 0.1\text{ L} = 100\text{ mL}$.
2. Concentration in grams per liter:
$$\text{Concentration} = \frac{90\text{ mg}}{1\text{ dL}} = \frac{0.090\text{ g}}{0.1\text{ L}} = 0.90\text{ g/L}$$
3. Molarity:
$$M = \frac{\text{Concentration in g/L}}{\text{Molar mass}} = \frac{0.90\text{ g/L}}{180\text{ g/mol}} = 0.005\text{ mol/L} = 5.0 \times 10^{-3}\text{ M}$$

questions.question: [NEET 2020] To prepare a $0.1\text{ M}$ solution of $\text{Na}_2\text{CO}_3$ in $100\text{ mL}$ volumetric flask, the mass of anhydrous sodium carbonate required is: (Molar mass of $\text{Na}_2\text{CO}_3 = 106\text{ g/mol}$)
questions.solution:
1. Moles required:
$$n = M \times V(\text{in L}) = 0.1\text{ mol/L} \times 0.100\text{ L} = 0.01\text{ mol}$$
2. Mass of $\text{Na}_2\text{CO}_3$ required:
$$m = n \times M_w = 0.01\text{ mol} \times 106\text{ g/mol} = 1.06\text{ g}$$

questions.question: [NEET 2022] Equal volumes of $0.1\text{ M } \text{NaCl}$ and $0.1\text{ M } \text{CaCl}_2$ solutions are mixed together. Assuming no precipitation occurs, the total molar concentration of chloride ions ($\text{Cl}^-$) in the mixture is:
questions.solution:
Let the volume of each solution mixed be $V\text{ mL}$:
1. Millimoles of $\text{Cl}^-$ from $\text{NaCl}$ (which yields $1\text{ Cl}^-$ per formula unit):
$$\text{mmol}(\text{Cl}^-)_1 = 0.1 \times 1 \times V = 0.1 V$$
2. Millimoles of $\text{Cl}^-$ from $\text{CaCl}_2$ (which yields $2\text{ Cl}^-$ per formula unit):
$$\text{mmol}(\text{Cl}^-)_2 = 0.1 \times 2 \times V = 0.2 V$$
3. Total millimoles of $\text{Cl}^-$:
$$\text{Total mmol} = 0.1 V + 0.2 V = 0.3 V$$
4. Total volume of mixture $= V + V = 2V\text{ mL}$.
5. Concentration of chloride ions:
$$[\text{Cl}^-] = \frac{0.3 V}{2V} = 0.15\text{ M}$$

questions.question: [NEET 2021] A gas mixture containing air has a carbon monoxide ($\text{CO}$) level of $8.0\text{ ppm}$ by volume. What volume of pure $\text{CO}$ is present in $1.0\text{ m}^3$ of this air at the same temperature and pressure?
questions.solution:
1. Volume of sample: $1.0\text{ m}^3 = 1000\text{ L} = 10^6\text{ mL}$.
2. By definition of parts per million by volume:
$$\text{ppm (v/v)} = \frac{\text{Volume of solute}}{\text{Total volume}} \times 10^6$$
$$8.0 = \frac{V_{\text{CO}}}{10^6\text{ mL}} \times 10^6 \implies V_{\text{CO}} = 8.0\text{ mL}$$

questions.question: [NEET 2023] A solution is prepared by dissolving $4.9\text{ g}$ of $\text{H}_2\text{SO}_4$ in water to make $500\text{ mL}$ of solution. The normality of this solution is: (Molar mass of $\text{H}_2\text{SO}_4 = 98\text{ g/mol}$)
questions.solution:
1. Equivalent mass of $\text{H}_2\text{SO}_4$:
$$E = \frac{M_w}{n\text{-factor}} = \frac{98}{2} = 49\text{ g/eq}$$
2. Number of gram equivalents of $\text{H}_2\text{SO}_4$:
$$\text{Gram equivalents} = \frac{4.9\text{ g}}{49\text{ g/eq}} = 0.10\text{ eq}$$
3. Normality ($N$):
$$N = \frac{\text{Gram equivalents}}{V(\text{in L})} = \frac{0.10\text{ eq}}{0.50\text{ L}} = 0.20\text{ N}$$

questions.question: [NEET 2020] When the temperature of an aqueous solution is raised from $20^\circ\text{C}$ to $50^\circ\text{C}$, which of the following concentration terms will DECREASE?
questions.solution:
1. As temperature increases, the solution expands, causing its volume to increase ($V_2 > V_1$).
2. Molarity is inversely proportional to volume:
$$M = \frac{n_{\text{solute}}}{V_{\text{solution}}}$$
As $V$ increases with temperature, the **molarity decreases**.
3. Molality, mole fraction, and mass percentage depend solely on mass, so they remain unaffected by temperature changes.

questions.question: [NEET 2022] In an aqueous solution of glucose, the mole fraction of glucose is $0.1$. The mass percentage of glucose in this solution is approximately: (Molar masses: $\text{Glucose} = 180\text{ g/mol}, \text{Water} = 18\text{ g/mol}$)
questions.solution:
Consider a mixture containing a total of $1.0\text{ mole}$ of components:
1. Moles of glucose $= 0.1\text{ mol}$.
2. Moles of water $= 1 - 0.1 = 0.9\text{ mol}$.
3. Masses of each component:
$$m_{\text{glucose}} = 0.1\text{ mol} \times 180\text{ g/mol} = 18.0\text{ g}$$
$$m_{\text{water}} = 0.9\text{ mol} \times 18\text{ g/mol} = 16.2\text{ g}$$
4. Total mass of solution:
$$m_{\text{solution}} = 18.0 + 16.2 = 34.2\text{ g}$$
5. Mass percentage of glucose:
$$\%\text{ glucose} = \frac{18.0}{34.2} \times 100 \approx 52.63\% \approx 52.6\%$$

questions.question: [NEET 2021] What is the molarity of a solution obtained by mixing $100\text{ mL}$ of $0.2\text{ M } \text{NaOH}$ with $100\text{ mL}$ of $0.1\text{ M } \text{HCl}$?
questions.solution:
1. Calculate initial millimoles:
$$\text{mmol of } \text{NaOH} = 100\text{ mL} \times 0.2\text{ M} = 20\text{ mmol}$$
$$\text{mmol of } \text{HCl} = 100\text{ mL} \times 0.1\text{ M} = 10\text{ mmol}$$
2. Neutralization reaction:
$$\text{NaOH} + \text{HCl} \rightarrow \text{NaCl} + \text{H}_2\text{O}$$
$10\text{ mmol of } \text{HCl}$ will neutralize $10\text{ mmol of } \text{NaOH}$.
3. Unreacted $\text{NaOH}$ remaining:
$$\text{Remaining mmol of } \text{NaOH} = 20 - 10 = 10\text{ mmol}$$
4. Total volume of mixture:
$$V_{\text{total}} = 100 + 100 = 200\text{ mL}$$
5. Molarity of unreacted $\text{NaOH}$:
$$M = \frac{10\text{ mmol}}{200\text{ mL}} = 0.05\text{ M}$$

questions.question: [NEET 2023] An aqueous solution of methanol ($\text{CH}_3\text{OH}$) is $5.0\text{ molal}$. If the density of the solution is $0.98\text{ g/mL}$, the molarity of the solution is: (Molar mass of $\text{CH}_3\text{OH} = 32.0\text{ g/mol}$)
questions.solution:
Using the standard conversion formula between molarity ($M$) and molality ($m$):
$$M = \frac{m \times d}{1 + \frac{m \times M_w}{1000}}$$
where $m = 5.0\text{ mol/kg}$, $d = 0.98\text{ g/mL}$, and $M_w = 32.0\text{ g/mol}$:
$$M = \frac{5.0 \times 0.98}{1 + \frac{5.0 \times 32.0}{1000}} = \frac{4.90}{1 + \frac{160}{1000}} = \frac{4.90}{1 + 0.16} = \frac{4.90}{1.16} \approx 4.224\text{ M} \approx 4.22\text{ M}$$

questions.question: [NEET 2020] A solution of cane sugar (sucrose, molar mass $= 342\text{ g/mol}$) is $3.42\%\ (w/v)$. The molarity of this solution is:
questions.solution:
1. A $3.42\%\ (w/v)$ solution contains $3.42\text{ g}$ of sucrose in $100\text{ mL}$ of solution.
2. Mass of sucrose in $1000\text{ mL}$ ($1\text{ L}$) of solution:
$$\text{Mass in } 1\text{ L} = 3.42 \times 10 = 34.2\text{ g/L}$$
3. Molarity:
$$M = \frac{34.2\text{ g/L}}{342\text{ g/mol}} = 0.10\text{ M}$$

questions.question: [NEET 2022] The mass of crystalline oxalic acid dihydrate ($(\text{COOH})_2 \cdot 2\text{H}_2\text{O}$) required to prepare $250\text{ mL}$ of a $0.1\text{ N}$ solution is: (Molar mass of dihydrate $= 126.0\text{ g/mol}$)
questions.solution:
1. Oxalic acid is a dibasic acid, so its $n$-factor is $2$.
2. Equivalent mass of $(\text{COOH})_2 \cdot 2\text{H}_2\text{O}$:
$$E = \frac{M_w}{2} = \frac{126.0}{2} = 63.0\text{ g/eq}$$
3. Mass required:
$$m = N \times E \times V(\text{in L}) = 0.1\text{ eq/L} \times 63.0\text{ g/eq} \times 0.250\text{ L} = 1.575\text{ g}$$

questions.question: [NEET 2021] A gas mixture contains equal moles of helium ($\text{He}$) and oxygen ($\text{O}_2$). What is the mass percentage of helium in the mixture? (Atomic masses: $\text{He} = 4\text{ u}, \text{O} = 16\text{ u}$)
questions.solution:
Consider $1.0\text{ mole}$ of each gas in the mixture:
1. Mass of $1.0\text{ mole}$ of $\text{He} = 4.0\text{ g}$.
2. Mass of $1.0\text{ mole}$ of $\text{O}_2 = 32.0\text{ g}$.
3. Total mass of mixture $= 4.0 + 32.0 = 36.0\text{ g}$.
4. Mass percentage of helium:
$$\%\text{ He} = \frac{4.0\text{ g}}{36.0\text{ g}} \times 100 = \frac{1}{9} \times 100 \approx 11.11\% \approx 11.1\%$$

questions.question: [NEET 2023] If $20\text{ mL}$ of $0.5\text{ M } \text{Ba(OH)}_2$ is required to neutralize $25\text{ mL}$ of an $\text{H}_3\text{PO}_4$ solution to form $\text{Ba}_3(\text{PO}_4)_2$, the molarity of the phosphoric acid solution is:
questions.solution:
The balanced chemical neutralization equation is:
$$3\text{Ba(OH)}_2 + 2\text{H}_3\text{PO}_4 \rightarrow \text{Ba}_3(\text{PO}_4)_2 + 6\text{H}_2\text{O}$$
From stoichiometry:
$$\frac{\text{mmol of } \text{Ba(OH)}_2}{3} = \frac{\text{mmol of } \text{H}_3\text{PO}_4}{2}$$
1. Calculate millimoles of $\text{Ba(OH)}_2$:
$$\text{mmol} = 20\text{ mL} \times 0.5\text{ M} = 10\text{ mmol}$$
2. Calculate millimoles of $\text{H}_3\text{PO}_4$:
$$\frac{10}{3} = \frac{M_{\text{acid}} \times 25}{2}$$
$$M_{\text{acid}} \times 25 = \frac{20}{3}$$
$$M_{\text{acid}} = \frac{20}{75} = \frac{4}{15} \approx 0.2667\text{ M} \approx 0.267\text{ M}$$

questions.question: [NEET 2020] In a laboratory, sea water was found to contain $65\text{ ppm}$ of bromide ions ($\text{Br}^-$). What mass of bromide ions is present in $500\text{ kg}$ of this sea water?
questions.solution:
1. Total mass of sample $= 500\text{ kg} = 5.0 \times 10^5\text{ g}$.
2. By definition of ppm:
$$\text{ppm} = \frac{\text{Mass of solute}}{\text{Mass of solution}} \times 10^6$$
$$65 = \frac{m_{\text{Br}^-}}{5.0 \times 10^5\text{ g}} \times 10^6$$
$$65 = m_{\text{Br}^-} \times 2 \implies m_{\text{Br}^-} = \frac{65}{2} = 32.5\text{ g}$$

questions.question: [NEET 2022] For a very dilute aqueous solution, which of the following approximations is valid?
options: Molarity is approximately equal to Molality ($M \approx m$)
Mole fraction is equal to Molarity ($X \approx M$)
Mass percentage is equal to Molarity
questions.solution:
1. In very dilute aqueous solutions, the amount of solute is negligible compared to the solvent (water).
2. The density of water is approximately $1.0\text{ g/mL}$ ($1.0\text{ kg/L}$).
3. Hence, the volume of $1.0\text{ L}$ of solution has a mass very close to $1000\text{ g}$ of pure water.
4. Therefore, the number of moles of solute in $1.0\text{ L}$ of solution (Molarity) is practically identical to the number of moles of solute in $1.0\text{ kg}$ of solvent (Molality):
$$M \approx m$$

questions.question: [NEET 2021] A sample of $\text{H}_2\text{O}_2$ solution is labeled as '10 volume'. What is the molarity of this $\text{H}_2\text{O}_2$ solution?
questions.solution:
By definition, '10 volume' means $1\text{ L}$ of $\text{H}_2\text{O}_2$ solution yields $10\text{ L}$ of $\text{O}_2$ gas at STP:
$$2\text{H}_2\text{O}_2(aq) \rightarrow 2\text{H}_2\text{O}(l) + \text{O}_2(g)$$
- $1\text{ mole of } \text{O}_2$ at STP $= 22.4\text{ L}$, produced from $2\text{ moles of } \text{H}_2\text{O}_2$.
$$\text{Volume strength} = 11.2 \times \text{Molarity}$$
$$\text{Molarity} = \frac{\text{Volume strength}}{11.2} = \frac{10}{11.2} \approx 0.8928\text{ M} \approx 0.89\text{ M}$$

questions.question: [NEET 2023] An antifreeze solution is prepared from $222.6\text{ g}$ of ethylene glycol ($\text{C}_2\text{H}_6\text{O}_2$) and $200\text{ g}$ of water. What is the molality of the solution? (Molar mass of ethylene glycol $= 62.0\text{ g/mol}$)
questions.solution:
1. Moles of ethylene glycol:
$$n = \frac{222.6\text{ g}}{62.0\text{ g/mol}} = 3.590\text{ mol}$$
2. Mass of water in kilograms:
$$W = \frac{200\text{ g}}{1000} = 0.200\text{ kg}$$
3. Molality:
$$m = \frac{3.590\text{ mol}}{0.200\text{ kg}} = 17.95\text{ m}$$

questions.question: [NEET 2020] What mass of pure sodium hydroxide ($\text{NaOH}$) must be dissolved in water to prepare $500\text{ mL}$ of a $0.25\text{ M}$ solution? (Molar mass of $\text{NaOH} = 40.0\text{ g/mol}$)
questions.solution:
1. Moles of $\text{NaOH}$ required:
$$n = M \times V = 0.25\text{ mol/L} \times 0.500\text{ L} = 0.125\text{ mol}$$
2. Mass of $\text{NaOH}$:
$$m = 0.125\text{ mol} \times 40.0\text{ g/mol} = 5.0\text{ g}$$

questions.question: [NEET 2022] In which of the following pairs of solutions are the molar concentrations of the cation identical?
questions.solution:
Evaluate cation concentration for each choice:
1. In $1.0\text{ M } \text{NaCl}$: $[\text{Na}^+] = 1.0 \times 1 = 1.0\text{ M}$.
In $0.5\text{ M } \text{Na}_2\text{SO}_4$: $[\text{Na}^+] = 0.5 \times 2 = 1.0\text{ M}$.
Both have identical $[\text{Na}^+] = 1.0\text{ M}$.
2. In B: $[\text{Ca}^{2+}] = 1.0\text{ M}$ vs $[\text{Na}^+] = 1.0\text{ M}$ (different cations).
3. In C: $[\text{Al}^{3+}] = 0.5\text{ M}$ vs $[\text{Fe}^{3+}] = 1.0\text{ M}$.
4. In D: $[\text{K}^+] = 2.0\text{ M}$ vs $[\text{K}^+] = 4.0\text{ M}$.
Thus, Option A has identical cation concentrations.

questions.question: [NEET 2021] An aqueous solution of acetic acid ($\text{CH}_3\text{COOH}$) is $2.0\text{ M}$ and has a density of $1.02\text{ g/mL}$. The mass percentage of acetic acid in the solution is: (Molar mass of $\text{CH}_3\text{COOH} = 60.0\text{ g/mol}$)
questions.solution:
Consider $1.0\text{ L}$ ($1000\text{ mL}$) of the solution:
1. Moles of $\text{CH}_3\text{COOH} = 2.0\text{ mol}$.
2. Mass of solute:
$$m_{\text{solute}} = 2.0\text{ mol} \times 60.0\text{ g/mol} = 120.0\text{ g}$$
3. Mass of $1000\text{ mL}$ of solution:
$$m_{\text{solution}} = 1000\text{ mL} \times 1.02\text{ g/mL} = 1020.0\text{ g}$$
4. Mass percentage:
$$\%\text{ by mass} = \frac{120.0\text{ g}}{1020.0\text{ g}} \times 100 \approx 11.76\%$$

questions.question: [NEET 2023] A fluoride ion concentration of $1.0\text{ ppm}$ in drinking water is beneficial in preventing tooth decay. How many milligrams of fluoride ion are present in $2.0\text{ L}$ of such drinking water? (Density of water $= 1.0\text{ g/mL}$)
questions.solution:
1. For dilute aqueous solutions, $1.0\text{ ppm} = 1.0\text{ mg/L}$.
2. In $2.0\text{ L}$ of water with a concentration of $1.0\text{ ppm}$:
$$\text{Mass of } \text{F}^- = 1.0\text{ mg/L} \times 2.0\text{ L} = 2.0\text{ mg}$$

questions.question: [NEET 2020] When $100\text{ mL}$ of $0.1\text{ M } \text{H}_2\text{SO}_4$ is added to $100\text{ mL}$ of $0.1\text{ M } \text{Ba(OH)}_2$, a white precipitate of $\text{BaSO}_4$ forms. What is the concentration of unreacted barium or sulfate ions in the supernatant solution? (Ignore solubility of $\text{BaSO}_4$)
questions.solution:
Reaction:
$$\text{H}_2\text{SO}_4 + \text{Ba(OH)}_2 \rightarrow \text{BaSO}_4 \downarrow + 2\text{H}_2\text{O}$$
1. $\text{mmol of } \text{H}_2\text{SO}_4 = 100 \times 0.1 = 10\text{ mmol}$.
2. $\text{mmol of } \text{Ba(OH)}_2 = 100 \times 0.1 = 10\text{ mmol}$.
3. Both reactants are present in an exact $1 : 1$ stoichiometric ratio.
4. Both $\text{Ba}^{2+}$ and $\text{SO}_4^{2-}$ precipitate completely as insoluble barium sulfate ($\text{BaSO}_4$), leaving neither in excess.
Thus, their concentration in the supernatant is $0\text{ M}$.

questions.question: [NEET 2022] A solution containing $8.0\text{ g}$ of a substance in $100\text{ g}$ of diethyl ether boils at a temperature higher than pure ether. The mole fraction of diethyl ether in this solution is $0.90$. The molar mass of the substance is: (Molar mass of diethyl ether $= 74\text{ g/mol}$)
questions.solution:
1. Moles of solvent (diethyl ether, $\text{C}_4\text{H}_{10}\text{O}$):
$$n_{\text{ether}} = \frac{100\text{ g}}{74\text{ g/mol}} \approx 1.3514\text{ mol}$$
2. Given mole fraction of ether $X_{\text{ether}} = 0.90$:
$$X_{\text{solute}} = 1 - 0.90 = 0.10$$
3. Since $\frac{n_{\text{solute}}}{n_{\text{ether}}} = \frac{X_{\text{solute}}}{X_{\text{ether}}} = \frac{0.10}{0.90} = \frac{1}{9}$:
$$n_{\text{solute}} = \frac{n_{\text{ether}}}{9} = \frac{1.3514}{9} \approx 0.15015\text{ mol}$$
4. Molar mass of solute:
$$M_w = \frac{\text{Mass}}{n_{\text{solute}}} = \frac{8.0\text{ g}}{0.15015\text{ mol}} \approx 53.28\text{ g/mol}$$

questions.question: [NEET 2021] What volume of $12.0\text{ M } \text{HCl}$ must be taken to prepare $500\text{ mL}$ of a $3.0\text{ M } \text{HCl}$ solution?
questions.solution:
Using the dilution equation:
$$M_1 V_1 = M_2 V_2$$
Substitute $M_1 = 12.0\text{ M}$, $M_2 = 3.0\text{ M}$, and $V_2 = 500\text{ mL}$:
$$12.0 \times V_1 = 3.0 \times 500$$
$$12.0 \times V_1 = 1500 \implies V_1 = \frac{1500}{12.0} = 125\text{ mL}$$

questions.question: [NEET 2023] A solution of glucose ($\text{C}_6\text{H}_{12}\text{O}_6$) in water is labeled as $10\%\ (w/w)$. If the density of this solution is $1.20\text{ g/mL}$, the molarity of the solution is: (Molar mass of glucose $= 180\text{ g/mol}$)
questions.solution:
Using the formula:
$$M = \frac{x \times d \times 10}{M_w}$$
Substitute $x = 10$, $d = 1.20\text{ g/mL}$, and $M_w = 180\text{ g/mol}$:
$$M = \frac{10 \times 1.20 \times 10}{180} = \frac{120}{180} = \frac{2}{3} \approx 0.667\text{ M} \approx 0.67\text{ M}$$

questions.question: [NEET 2020] What is the molality of an aqueous solution of urea if the mole fraction of urea is $0.05$? (Molar mass of water $= 18.0\text{ g/mol}$)
questions.solution:
Using the relation between molality and mole fraction:
$$m = \frac{X_{\text{solute}}}{1 - X_{\text{solute}}} \times \frac{1000}{M_{\text{solvent}}}$$
Substitute $X_{\text{solute}} = 0.05$ and $M_{\text{solvent}} = 18.0\text{ g/mol}$:
$$m = \frac{0.05}{1 - 0.05} \times \frac{1000}{18} = \frac{0.05}{0.95} \times 55.555$$
$$m = \frac{1}{19} \times 55.555 \approx 2.924\text{ m} \approx 2.92\text{ m}$$
